purpose: Find an actual paired work/area datum before more engineering or a historical fit. The Heroninos candidate just screened is closed and must not be reopened through an expanding bibliography.
candidate_family: Roman Egyptian cereal reaping contracts or documented work-performance agreements, identified by original publication and primary record. This is a proposed alternative target family, not an already qualified observation or a covert ploughing-rate dataset.
scope: At most three targeted searches and two source bodies (one original scholarly/source-method discussion and one explicitly identified primary record, or two directly identified primary records). Prefer dates nearAD200; retain exact chronology, region, crop and institutional context. Reserved workbook/Buringh pools and climate remain closed.
eligibility: Require matching worked/contracted area, defined operation, crew/exposure or explicit performance requirement and time unit on the same event. Distinguish promised minimum performance, paid worker-days and actually completed work. Do not turn a start date, deadline, named people or wage sum into elapsed work or a workforce census.
fit_scope_rule: The first proposed estimand was plough-operator days per area. A qualifying reaping target would require an explicit new estimand/likelihood or inequality-bound declaration before fitting; it must not be labelled a plough or annual draft-capacity calibration. A contractual requirement can constrain a scenario but is not automatically an observed realized rate.
decision: Return one traceable matched observation/constraint with eligibility limits or a finite no-fit closure. No model run or optimizer before baseline/target/estimand/evaluation uses align. Do not add generic resource adapters or task-unit checks in place of the datum.
